methodology.request_accounting: request-level-v1 where a transcript reconciles; otherwise legacy session allocation
methodology.note: Request-level activity is the primary operation of a request. It is associated with the request context, not proven to have caused every token in it.

github_workflows.workflow: Check cloud/ is up to date

task.note: Session task ids are recorded but are not one explicit development task per session; they are reported separately from explicit task metadata.

issue.note: Issue attribution is independent of activity classification. An Unknown activity is not an unattributed issue.

outcome.verified_note: A successful command or a model claim is not a verified task outcome; evidence review remains human.

repetition.note: A repetition is the same command, revision, patch, environment and result signature. A repeated success may be a deliberate repeatability check; a repeated failure may be a real iteration. Inspect before calling either waste.

reconciliation.method: Provider message id deduplication; a session is counted from request events only when the request sum equals the session sum.

provenance.note: Prompt metadata only by default. Artifact references are not evidence that a model received or read the contents; raw prompt text is opt-in and local.

exploration.note: Repeated lookups are diagnostics, not proof of waste: a file may have changed, a test may have failed, or a new task may need the same evidence. Targets stay local.

tokens.note: Provider-reported token counts; estimated prompt bytes are kept separate and are never shown as exact tokens.

cost.note: Client-reported estimates may reflect subscription allowance, not an invoice. Per-request cost is derived from the session cost-state by token share and is labelled estimated. Missing cost is not zero.

cpu.note: CPU-seconds are measured by the process wrapper, or derived from sampled container percentages. They are not hardware cycle counts.

memory.note: Peak RSS and container peaks are different measurements; PHP peak is per request.

github.note: Durations and conclusions come from the GitHub API; billable minutes and runner CPU are unavailable.

opportunities.heading: A material share of request context is associated with code exploration
opportunities.recommendation: When a lookup needs several reads, try `node scripts/code-map.mjs <env|folder> <symbol|file>` once before a grep/sed chain; compare the next comparable session before changing instructions.
opportunities.limitations: Request context is associated with the primary activity, not proven to be caused by it. Complex accessibility work may legitimately need this exploration.

opportunities.heading: A material share of request context has no reliable activity classification
opportunities.recommendation: Inspect the reason breakdown in the Unknown view. Model-only requests have no tool evidence; unrecognized commands need a registry rule; compound commands need a clearer script or a narrower single-purpose call.
opportunities.limitations: Unknown is not waste. It is a measurement gap and can be reduced only by better evidence, not by relabelling.

opportunities.heading: Several sessions start or average a large context
opportunities.recommendation: Measure the starting context with `node scripts/context-size.mjs` before changing AGENTS.md, skills or memory files. The client re-reads context on every call, so a smaller start can matter more than a single large result.
opportunities.limitations: A large context is not waste by itself; it may carry essential evidence. The existing 2026-10-15 option-C work already reduced AGENTS.md from 8.6k to 2.9k tokens.

opportunities.heading: The same environment work appears more than once

measurement.unit: activity events with the same activity, variant and commit

opportunities.recommendation: Check whether the environment was unchanged before re-running Composer, cache rebuild or setup; `setup.mjs` is resumable and `lab-env.mjs status` shows what exists.
opportunities.limitations: An activity label does not prove the work was redundant; a failed or partial build can legitimately need a rerun.

opportunities.heading: Some GitHub Actions runs overlap a later run
opportunities.recommendation: Review whether a push triggered CI that a later push made obsolete. Concurrency groups and a short debounce can reduce this; do not cancel a run that is producing needed evidence.
opportunities.limitations: Overlap is inferred from GitHub timestamps. A run may have been useful despite a later run.

opportunities.heading: Some sessions repeat a lookup target
opportunities.recommendation: Check whether the target changed, a test failed, or the second lookup crossed a task boundary. Prefer one `code-map.mjs` call when a symbol must be located and read; do not suppress a necessary re-read after an edit.
opportunities.limitations: The client transcript records the target and order, not the reason. A repeated lookup after a patch or a new revision can be necessary.

privacy.public_fields: Aggregates and grouped rows only; no transcript titles, paths, prompts, responses, task descriptions, evidence references, API keys, account ids or precise work timestamps.
privacy.raw_ledger: Local-only ledger; not committed and not published.

limitations: AI token and cost values are only as complete as the local Claude Code transcripts and recorded model-eval trials. Other agents and API clients are not represented yet.

Cost is a client-reported estimate (or an estimate where no provider cost exists), not an invoice or subscription statement. Per-request cost is derived from the session estimate by token share. Missing cost is null, never zero.

Request-level activity is associated with the context processed at that request; it is not proof that the activity caused every token. Legacy session rows use a different method and are not directly comparable.
Unknown is a measurement gap, not waste. Tool-free requests have no tool-based activity evidence; unrecognized inline code and unsupported clients remain explicitly Unknown.

Prompt and artifact provenance is metadata-only by default. The effective provider request, hidden instructions and client-added attachments are only partly observable; a reference does not prove ingestion.

CPU-seconds come from measured processes, or are derived from sampled Docker percentages. They are not hardware cycle counts and do not include host-wide work such as Mutagen, the DDEV router or the OS.
GitHub Actions duration comes from the API; billable minutes and runner CPU are unavailable. Overlap/supersession is inferred.
The collector runs on demand; a period with no events is not proof that no work happened.
Recorded duration is the sum of event spans and may include idle time; it is not active development time.
This report does not claim that lower resource use means lower energy use or emissions.
